column1: # How a character talks, for the retranslation. Hand-written; this is the file
# to edit. modules/ScenePrompt.js puts the rows for a scene's own cast into its
# prompt, keyed by the English name the cast line carries -- the same key
# glossaries/character_genders.md uses, so a name has to be spelled the way that
# table spells it or nothing is found.
# Columns: the English name <TAB> how they speak <TAB> where it came from.
# This is about the voice and nothing else. Who somebody is, what they have
# done and who they love are in the two sources below and are not repeated
# here: a prompt has room for one line per speaker and the line has to be the
# Both sources are read rather than remembered, in this order:
#   card    archives/Rance10EX_v1_04/9_カード情報.x, コメント１-５ -- the game's
#           own description of 302 named characters, already in English. The
#           authority, and often about their history rather than their manner.
#   wiki    the "Personality and Appearance" section of their page on the
#           AliceSoft wiki. Longer, and about the whole series rather than this
#           game, so where it disagrees with the card the card wins.
#   asked   neither settled it and a person decided.
# The Japanese says it too, on every line: the pronoun (俺様 against 私), the
# politeness, the sentence-final particle. A translator reading the scene has
# that in front of them, which is why this file is a summary and not a rule --
# it says what to listen for, and the line itself says the rest.
# 417 speakers have a line in the game and 24 of them say half of it. This file
# is written from the top down and an entry missing is the normal case, not a
# fault: the prompt prints the rows it has.

column2: Blunt, loud, crude. Gives orders and never asks; brags, mocks, and says exactly what he wants. Calls Sill his slave and means it. Never polite, never elaborate, never embarrassed.

Unfailingly polite and soft-spoken -- ですます to everyone, "Rance-sama" every time. Meek, apologetic, easily flustered and easily frightened, and cheerful about serving anyway. Never sarcastic, never coarse.

Loud, casual and unguarded -- 俺 and お前, dropped endings, an exclamation or a yelp on most lines. El's best friend and the one who says out loud what everyone else is thinking: panics, jokes, gawks at women, complains. Familiar with everyone, deferential to nobody, and never formal.

Imperious and short-fused -- barks orders, drops her first-person pronoun almost entirely, and calls everyone お前 or 貴様. Contemptuous of humans and quick to threaten; "-sama" only for Hornet. Comes apart into stammering and yelping the moment she is hurt or touched, and hates that it shows.

A cheerful small child: short sentences, plain words, "-chan" and "-san" for everybody, easy laughter and her father's gahaha. Warm and unguarded with strangers, and blunt to the point of scolding adults when she thinks they are wrong. Never sarcastic, never coarse.

Rough and arrogant, a prince who talks like a street thug -- 俺様, slurred and clipped endings, がはははは. Gives orders, brags, picks fights, never softens a word. The one exception is anything to do with sex, where he stammers and bluffs.

Grandiose and theatrical: 余 for herself, everyone else a subject or a minion, and a booming laugh over everything. Lectures at length, delights in her own knowledge, takes flattery as her due. Even a defeat is announced as something she intended all along.

Polite ですます, flat and very short -- statements of fact with nothing attached to them, often two or three words. So deadpan that nobody can tell when she is joking, and shameless about anything embarrassing. Calls Rance by name alone, no honorific.

Bellowing and savage -- 俺様, てめぇ, verbs spat out with ～やがる, and laughter or screams stretched across a whole line. Gloats over cruelty and threatens constantly. Flips instantly into fawning servility in front of anyone stronger than he is.

Chirpy exposition delivered at the audience rather than at the room -- addresses あなた directly, announces her own section headings, drags her vowels out. A gushing Rance obsessive, so a briefing keeps derailing into fangirling. Never grave for long, even about the end of the world.

Playful and childlike -- giggles, drawn-out vowels, teasing nicknames, "onee-sama" for Shizuka. Clingy and affectionate with the family, easily embarrassed. Her memories are gone, so nothing of the cold, murderous Nagi of the earlier games is left in how she talks.

Courteous and measured -- 僕, careful complete sentences, "-sama" for others, no raised voice. A young lord who thinks before speaking and takes responsibility for everyone in the room. Warms a little with family, and only Zance can needle him into sounding his age.

Calm, courteous ですます, and organised -- states the situation, then what is to be done about it. Leads without raising her voice and is never visibly rattled in front of others. Names people rather than pointing at them, and is quietly warm with those she trusts: a soft laugh rather than a joke.

An ordinary girl's casual speech, never as ninja-like as she is trying to sound -- 私, half-finished sentences, sighs, and a great deal of flustered stammering. Complains, panics and talks herself down constantly; visibly delighted on the rare occasion somebody praises her.

Curt and irritable -- 私, あんた for everyone including Rance, orders given as flat imperatives. Says what she thinks of people to their faces, has no patience for stupidity, and never softens a refusal. Warmer only with Maria and with her own family.

Kansai through and through -- うち for herself, "-han" where others say "-san", and the whole や／へん／あかん register. Brash, fast, teasing, and forever counting money out loud. She needs a broad, informal English voice of her own; neutral English loses the whole character.

Bookish and correct -- proper vocabulary, careful constructions, a fondness for the right way of doing things. Serious and easily irritated: あんた and a snapped retort when provoked, then straight back to lecturing. Stiff and flustered around anything romantic.

Rustic and humble -- a country dialect (おら, ～だす, ～だども) and "Rance-sama" every other line. Cheerful, grateful and self-effacing however badly he is treated, quick to tears of joy, tongue-tied when praised. Plain, warm, uneducated English rather than neutral English.

A staff officer's ですます: numbers, assessments and recommendations, delivered without decoration. Correct and professional with everybody, and gives herself away only in a sigh or a clipped word when she is overruled or patronised. Proud of her work and stung when it is ignored.

An old man's voice coming out of a sword -- 儂, ～じゃ／～のう, "boy" and "you there" for people. Chatty, cheerful and relentlessly lewd, egging Rance on and passing judgement on every woman in sight. Whines theatrically the moment he is told to shut up.

Timid and halting -- stammered openings, sentences that trail off, an apology before and after. Softens every request into a question and needs reassurance to keep going. Opens into ordinary bright teenage chatter only with people she already trusts.

Casual and warm -- 私, relaxed feminine endings, sighs and "geez". Brightens the moment the subject is machinery and will explain her own inventions at length. Grumbles at Rance's schemes and goes along with them anyway.

A tournament announcer at the microphone -- polite ですます, play-by-play in the past tense, sound effects, and a build-up before every reveal. Breezy and friendly off the mic, professionally neutral about who wins while making it perfectly obvious who she is rooting for.

Not one character but the game's generic plate for a Monster Army officer, so the exact register moves from scene to scene. Brutal and contemptuous by default -- 貴様 down at humans, threats and boasts, no eloquence and no courtesy for its own sake -- but clipped and deferential up the chain of command, and outright panic when reporting a disaster.
